[MUQATIL:2:286/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God requires a person to do only what that person is capable of doing.
[MUQATIL:2:286/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | A person receives the good they earn and bears the sin they commit.
[MUQATIL:2:286/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | Gabriel taught Muhammad this plea: do not punish us for ignorance or error that made us leave God’s command; God answered, “That is granted to you.”
[MUQATIL:2:286/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Iṣr means a covenant; the plea asks not to burden this community as God burdened Israel, forbidding camel meat, sheep fat, and all cloven-hoofed animals because of their sins, and making them apes and pigs.
[MUQATIL:2:286/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | “Pardon us” asks God to pardon, and “forgive us” asks Him to overlook all their sins.
[MUQATIL:2:286/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God is their protector; they ask victory over disbelievers of Mecca and elsewhere until Resurrection. God grants the requests, intercedes for the community, and exempts it for error, forgetfulness, and coercion, a favor withheld from earlier nations.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرمنأبوابإن)#508/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With conditional إن, an elliptical pattern such as إن خيرا فخير is carried on a verb because a noun cannot directly begin after إن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A participle after a noun may be an agreeing adjective or an accusative predicate attached to the implicit noun after معه or عنده; its intended attachment determines the case.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In the construction with the horse riding a mule, the participle cannot be an adjective; it is only a predicate in the accusative.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | For paired, enduring qualities, adjective agreement is stronger; accusative is possible but suggests a temporary state rather than two coequal traits.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | rejects | Sībawayh rejects the proposed inverted-order analysis (qalb), since it gives the wrong case and fails on the cited adjective constructions.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With a participle describing the vocative, an overt agent such as Zayd cannot be attached as its adjective; an agent like the addressee’s father can be construed separately, and pronoun placement affects case.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In rab rajul wa-akhīhi, the genitive brother is understood as an indefinite brother belonging to a man; this construction is weak and requires an indefinite to precede it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In the line “أي فتى هيجاء أنت وجارها,” جارها must be genitive: the poet praises the war’s young man and its neighbor, not a specific man joined in the praise.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابإجراءالصفةفيهعلىالاسمفيبعضالمواضعأحسن)#222/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Aʿshā’s couplet about dunes and their ridges is cited as poetic evidence for the unusual genitive coordination in rab rajul wa-akhīhi.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A fa-following subjunctive takes implicit أن; otherwise the verb coordinates with the first or occupies a nominal or predicate position.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لا تأتينا فتحدثنا إلا ازددنا فيك رغبة has the same causal construction as ما تأتيني فتحدثني; al-Laʿīn’s poem gives a parallel.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لا يسعني شيء فيعجز عنك means nothing can contain me and then be unable for you; coordination would assert the unintended opposite.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما أنت منا فتحدثنا cannot coordinate with ما because the preceding phrase is nominal; nominative can start a clause, as in Farazdaq’s ما أنت من قيس فتنبح دونها.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ألا ماء فأشربه and ليته عندنا فيحدثنا take subjunctive because the following verb is not coordinated; Umayya’s ألا رسول لنا منا فيخبرنا is parallel.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ألا تقع الماء فتسبح can be coordinated as ألا تسبح or take subjunctive as if ‘there be a fall, then you swim’; swimming follows the fall.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After ألم تأتنا, the fa-verb is subjunctive when uncoordinated and jussive when shared; ألم تسأل فتخبرك الرسوم is a poetic example.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لا تمددها فتشقها is subjunctive when uncoordinated, as is the Qur’anic لا تفتروا على الله كذبا فيسحتكم بعذاب; a coordinated form can be jussive. | mentions 20:61
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An imperative cannot directly govern a jussive imperfect because its form is fixed; use a lām command, as in ائته فليحدثك.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ألست قد أتيتنا فتحدثنا is subjunctive if telling follows from coming, but nominative if the meaning is ‘and you told us’; كأنك لم تأتنا فتحدثنا is jussive when coordinated.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In لا تأتيني فتحدثني, a causal reading makes the first event nominal, so the following verb cannot attach directly; implicit أن makes it nominal too.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حسبته شتمني فأثب عليه is subjunctive if the leap is hypothetical; if it already occurred, use nominative.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Khalil allows nominative in ائتني فأحدثك when it means ‘come; I will talk whether or not you come,’ not that coming causes talk; al-Nābigha’s rain poem similarly resumes a report after a prayer.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Sībawayh reports that Yūnus heard the ruins verse with ألم, where the ruins speak independently; elsewhere in the same passage Yūnus is named as reciter of al-Aʿshā’s poem.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Aʿshā’s ثمت لا تجزونني ... ولكن سيجزيني الإله فيعقبا is nominative because the first clause is affirmative and the next resumes a report.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In affirmative contexts fa does not suppress أن and only nominative is ordinarily used; فلا تكفر فيتعلمون and كن فيكون are resumptive, not causal. | mentions 2:102, 2:117
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetic necessity can allow subjunctive in an affirmative clause by implicit أن, but Sībawayh calls it weak in ordinary speech; he cites an unnamed poet, al-Aʿshā, and Ṭarafa.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f26] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو عمرو | reports | Abū ʿAmr used لا تأتنا فنشتمك as an example in the discussion of fa after a negative command.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f27] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yūnus explains ما أتيتني فأحدثك فيما أستقبل as ‘if you come, I will talk and honor you in the future,’ like a noncausal ائتني فأحدثك.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f28] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yūnus calls ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فتصبح الأرض مخضرة affirmative and informative; the coming is affirmed, unlike negative examples. | mentions 22:63
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f29] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما تأتيني فتحدثني does not deny speech; it says only that failure to come prevents the talk.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Farazdaq’s and Zuhayr’s lines illustrate how a relation or particle required by an initial expression can be understood across what follows without being repeated.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f30] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After an affirmed clause such as قد كان عندنا فسوف يأتينا فيحدثنا, the fa-verb is nominative, coordinated or independent; goal meanings do not apply.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f31] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Fa is compared with حتى in taking implicit أن where the meaning is a goal, and with the lām in ما كان ليفعل.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Fa-nasb has several meanings, all with implicit أن; matching another verb’s case does not make the meanings identical.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما تأتيني فتحدثني can mean ‘if you came, I would speak,’ ‘you never come without not speaking,’ or coordination of both negatives; the first reading denies coming, not speech.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا exemplifies subjunctive, while هذا يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون exemplifies nominative coordination. | mentions 43:75, 77:35, 77:36
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nominative can begin a new nominal clause, as in the Hārithī poem فنرجى ونكثر التأميلا, understood as فنحن نرجى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | ما أتيتنا فتحدثنا normally has subjunctive on a causal reading; nominative is possible by linking to the syntactic position of أتيتنا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/f9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما تأتينا فتكلم إلا بالجميل means that if you came, you would speak only well; raising coordinates the clauses. Farazdaq’s فينطق إلا بالتي هي أعرف is a poetic parallel.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When an earlier verb governs the construction, a follo

wing coordinated noun may be accusative by the verb’s underlying object relation, even if the first phrase is prepositional.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After حتى, accusative is preferred when the following phrase continues the preceding verb, whether the first object is nominative, accusative, or genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حتى may mark a limit and govern genitive while the noun remains an underlying object, as in هذا ضارب القوم حتى زيدا يضربه.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | After هلك القوم حتى زيدا أهلكته, accusative is preferred because the item continues the verb-based construction even when the preceding phrase is genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Case follows semantic object status rather than only surface case: a prepositional object can be accusative in meaning, while a topical subject may still license accusative continuation by its predicate relation.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl analyzes the noun after the preposition as accusative in position and meaning, despite the overt preposition.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A noun after حتى may also be raised as a new topic, with its following clause as predicate; this parallels ordinary topical sentences.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | If the phrase after حتى contains no verb, only nominative is available, as in حتى زيد ملقى or حتى زيد مسرح.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ibn Marwān’s verse ألقى الصحيفة ... حتى نعله ألقاها is cited as poetic evidence for the construction after حتى.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Jarīr’s بمثل بني بدر and al-Aʿajjāj’s وغورا غائرا illustrate accusative coordination after prepositional phrases through the underlying meanings come and traverse.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A verb that only takes a prepositional complement cannot be omitted, since the preposition itself cannot be elided.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أما and إذا restart the clause, so a later item does not coordinate with an earlier one as it can after ثم or فاء.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | إن is not a verb: it has no implicit subject and does not allow the same word order as a verb, although it resembles one in its work.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما in exclamatory ما أحسن عبد الله governs like a verb but lacks verbal inflection, subject behavior, and word-order flexibility; لدن and كم likewise govern without being verbs.
[SIBAWAYH:أىذلكفعلتجازفإنحملتهعلىالاسمالذىبنىعليهالفعلكانبمنزلته#54/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حتى behaves like واو, فاء, and ثم for accusative coordination, but unlike أما it depends on the preceding clause and cannot begin one.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When المسكين refers to the speaker or addressee, it cannot be an appositive that leaves the referent uncertain; use the accusative construction or a fresh nominative instead.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The two accepted constructions for compassionate naming express the same meaning despite differing in form.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Insults can use facts already known to the listener: ʿUrwa’s “عداة الله من كذب وزور” and al-Nābigha’s “وجوه قرود” exemplify abusive descriptions.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus reports hearing al-Farazdaq recite the aunt-and-aunt poem as an insult; Sībawayh also says the nominative continuation is valid Arabic.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh says Hassān’s comparison of the people’s bodies and minds enumerates their traits rather than insulting them.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil allows the same Hassān phrase to be construed as an insult, with its epithet accusative under an omitted verb.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An accusative modifier can simply identify someone, without praise or blame: محصن is named with an explicit “I mean” verb, not an omitted boast or insult.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | holds | In expressions of compassion, المسكين may be a genitive appositive, an accusative object of an understood verb, or a nominative fresh comment; the poet’s البائسا supplies an example.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | rejects | Yunus argues merciful epithets simply match the preceding syntax and rejects an omitted noun for nominative examples; Sībawayh attributes that raised analysis to al-Khalil and Ibn Abi Ishaq.
[SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأنيكررهولايعرفكشيئاتنكره#230/f9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Khalil’s construction إنه المسكين أحمق inserts a nominative epithet between subject and predicate, but Sībawayh calls this analysis weak.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An adjective following an indefinite noun takes its case and forms a semantic unit with it; the qualification narrows the referent to the subset sharing that description.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس والخليل | reports | Yunus and al-Khalil allow these construct adjectives to become definite in some contexts, as in ضاربك used like صاحبك.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حسن الوجه is an exception: it remains indefinite unless marked with the definite article, as in هذا الحسن الوجه.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | إما قائم وإما قاعد says the person is in one of two states while leaving which state uncertain and excluding a third state such as reclining.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With two predicates, و does not itself order the actions; ف marks the second as immediately following, whereas ثم marks a later action after an interval.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أو ساجد offers one of two alternatives like إما, while لا ساجد removes doubt or emphasizes certainty and بل ساجد corrects a slip or mistaken first description.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حسن الوجه جميلة is possible because حسن describes the particular face and جميل describes that same special attribute; a general quality would instead use matching general adjectives.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | رجل صدق means a sound or righteous man and رجل سوء a corrupt man; neither phrase refers to truthfulness of speech or to having caused harm.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | رجلين مثلين means each man resembles the other; رجلين مثلك can mean each resembles you or that the pair together resembles you.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When one noun is split between contrasting qualities, as in رجلين مسلم وكافر, the modifiers can be parsed as adjectives, badals, or nominative answers depending on the implied question.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Expressions such as أيما رجل qualify an indefinite by completeness; حسبك من رجل and similar forms describe one who is fully sufficient or adequate.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | رجل راكع وساجد describes one person with both predicates, unlike مسلم وكافر after two people, which divides the qualities across the individuals.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus says مررت برجل مسلم وثلاثة رجال مسلمين takes genitive only because the noun and its adjective form one unit; raising would wrongly suggest a divided predicate.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With several different head nouns and one plural adjective, as in رجل وامرأة وحمار قيام, the adjective groups the nouns together; a divided reading would change the syntax.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In مررت بأربعة صريع و

جريح, the adjectives describe portions of the group, meaning some are slain and some wounded; they may also be parsed as apposition or a fresh explanation.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | مثل رجلين can measure the described man by song or portion, while مثل رجل أسدا means lion-like in strength and courage; Sibawayh calls the latter weak and inelegant.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A second adjective after بل can replace the first as a correction; لكن can make this repair after negation, but not after an affirmative clause.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r27] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | بل, ولا بل, and لكن can link two adjectives under one noun, like و, ف, ثم, أو, ولا, and إما.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r28] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus rejects genitive after فكيف in ما مررت برجل مسلم فكيف رجل راغب, since كيف begins a new construction and has no omitted noun after it.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r29] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | For هذا جحر ضب خرب, most and best Arabic uses nominative because خرب modifies جحر; some use genitive, explained either by treating the phrase as one unit or by attraction to the preceding genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | مثلك can qualify an indefinite by likeness or equality, including likeness of appearance; similar forms such as ضربك and نحوك work alike.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r30] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Khalil explains that dual جحرا ضب خربان avoids confusing the adjective with the possessor; Sibawayh sees the two explanations as equally valid, with number and gender sometimes causing mistaken agreement.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus treats هذا مثلك as definite when مثلك precedes the name and as indefinite when it follows; Sibawayh says some Arabs agree.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | شر منك marks a lesser degree than the comparison point, while خير منك marks a greater degree.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | غيرك distinguishes the described person from the one added after غير; آخر likewise marks another or separate individual.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حسن الوجه describes the indefinite through the quality of its own face, without the pronoun suffix found in حسن وجهه; the genitive phrase itself is adjectival.
[SIBAWAYH:فأماالنعتالذىجرىعلىالمنعوتفقولكمررتبرجلظريفقبلفصارالنعت#200/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A construct phrase attached to a definite noun can still function as an indefinite adjective when modifying, predicating, or naming an indefinite.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A verbal noun is nominative when its own verb governs it and the verb is not occupied by another object; it answers a question about the kind of action.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A verbal noun replacing a verb may take the definite article, as in السير and العراك, but a circumstantial verbal noun cannot.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Rāʿī's طرحا emphasizes that the rider lowers his gaze; it is an accusative verbal noun confirming the described action.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a verbal noun is intended to mean an event or matter rather than the action itself, it is nominative: خوف means a thing feared and قول a thing said.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms such as مضرب and مسرح can function as verbal nouns equivalent to ضرب and تسريح, and can follow the same case patterns.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Jarir's مسرحي القوافي means تسريحي القوافي, so مسرح is used as an action noun.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The forms معصية and موجدة can likewise function as verbal nouns corresponding to عصيان and وجد.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Ibn Ahmar's محربا is cited alongside قتلا as an action noun, supporting this verbal-noun use.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | مذهب and مسلك here denote a route or place, not the acts of going and following, so they are not verbal nouns.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A derived form can denote time or place: مضربها means the time of mating, and مبعث الجيوش and مضرب الشول are temporal.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Hamid ibn Thawr's مغار ابن همام denotes a time, which is why it is treated as an adverbial.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Without an adjective, a nominative verbal noun means a kind or instance of the action, as though some travel or striking occurred.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The verbal noun may be accusative when the verb is occupied by another object; the construction still specifies the action.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A question with كم may be answered by a dual verbal noun, although the expression compresses the underlying meaning because blows themselves are not struck.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Sībawayh reports an Arab's بسط عليه مرتان, meaning that punishment was inflicted twice.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With طوران طور كذا وطور كذا, nominative is preferred and accusative is very weak unless something is elided.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Expressions such as مرتين, طورين, and ضربتين can instead mark periods or durations, functioning as time adverbs.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An action noun can be accusative as a circumstantial description, as in walking or patient killing; an adjective can describe it in that role.
[SIBAWAYH:فيرتفعكماينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبهوينتصبإذاشغلتالفعلبغيره#89/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Alternatively, an accusative verbal noun can replace an unspoken repeated verb, like الحذر الحذر; this is good Arabic.
[SIBAWAYH:لأنهمفعولمعهومفعولبهكماانتصبنفسهفىقولكامرأونفسه|وذلك#115/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With waw, the following noun may be an object of accompaniment or an object; the waw leaves the sense intact while the preceding governor assigns its case, as the examples and poetry show.
[SIBAWAYH:لأنهمفعولمعهومفعولبهكماانتصبنفسهفىقولكامرأونفسه|وذلك#115/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ما زلت وزيدا the second noun is an object, paraphrasable as ما زلت بزيد; by contrast, ما زلت أسير والنيل means travelling with the Nile.
[SIBAWAYH:لأنهمفعولمعهومفعولبهكماانتصبنفسهفىقولكامرأونفسه|وذلك#115/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Do not coordinate a noun with an implicit nominative pronoun in a command such as اقعد وأخوك; make the pronoun explicit first.
[SIBAWAYH:لأنهمفعولمعهومفعولبهكماانتصبنفسهفىقولكامرأونفسه|وذلك#115/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Once the subject pronoun is explicit, the second element may follow either the first element's grammatical form or its meaning.
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A supplementary description may follow the first noun as an agreeing adjective, or be detached and started as a nominative sentence; accusative praise is another construction.
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A speaker may identify someone through an added name as though the listener had asked who the person was, even when no question was spoken.
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetic examples show that the following epithet can agree with the first noun or restart independently; al-Kharnq’s الطيبون parallels المؤتون, while Ibn Khayyat illustrates a new nominative phrase. | mentions 4:162
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus reports Arabic usage with both nominative and accusative epithets, including النازلون ... والطيبين and الظاعنون ... والقائلين; he also permits genitive coordination in مررت بزيد أخيك وصاحبك, citing a rajaz line.
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · عيسى | reports | Isa reports hearing Dhu al-Rumma recite the cited descriptive phrase in the accusative.
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | holds | A

l-Khalil analyzes accusative praise as an unspoken verb such as “I mention,” used when the audience already knows the fact; the verb is not normally made explicit, as in boastful tribal declarations.
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | holds | A derogatory supplementary description such as “شعثا” can be accusative through an unspoken “I mention them,” though it may instead be attached as a genitive adjective.
[SIBAWAYH:وإنشئتجعلتهصفةفجرىعلىالأولوإنشئتقطعتهفابتدأته|وذلكقولك#228/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Praise requires a fitting description and a listener able to recognize its subject; not every person or quality can bear the same exalted praise, and divine honor language does not transfer unchanged to people.
[SIBAWAYH:والترخيمحذفأواخرالأسماءالمفردةتخفيفاكماحذفواغيرذلكمن#325/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Tarḫīm deletes the ending of a singular name for ease; it is normally limited to frequent vocatives, with poetic necessity as an exception.
[SIBAWAYH:والترخيمحذفأواخرالأسماءالمفردةتخفيفاكماحذفواغيرذلكمن#325/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A genitive complement or descriptor is not addressed; constructs and tanwīn-marked vocatives retain their forms.
[SIBAWAYH:والترخيمحذفأواخرالأسماءالمفردةتخفيفاكماحذفواغيرذلكمن#325/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Deleting the possessive yāʾ in يا زيد removes an iḍāfa ending, not the name’s final letter; deletion reaches only the name’s actual end.
[SIBAWAYH:والترخيمحذفأواخرالأسماءالمفردةتخفيفاكماحذفواغيرذلكمن#325/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A genitive mustaghāth is like a genitive complement, a mandūb already has its marker, and a dual is like tanwīn; none is additionally truncated.
[SIBAWAYH:والترخيمحذفأواخرالأسماءالمفردةتخفيفاكماحذفواغيرذلكمن#325/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The final surviving letter keeps its original vowel or pause because tarḫīm removes the inflectional ending for this vocative use.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بنو تميم | reports | Tamim leaves ما syntactically inactive; Sībawayh calls this the analogical treatment because ما is not a verb and has no implicit subject.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When the predicate precedes its subject, ما requires the nominative; it cannot behave fully like a verb, and its order is less flexible than verbal constructions.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما زيد إلا منطلق works alike in both dialects; the Qur’anic ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا shows that ما weakens when negation is narrowed by exception. | mentions 36:15
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ما does not govern strongly when it reverses the sense of ليس, just as it weakens when the predicate is fronted.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ما كان, ما negates كان; in ليس زيد إلا ذاهبا, ما would instead add an affirmative force to the negation.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With ما, the second negative predicate may be raised as a fresh clause or accusative when coordinated with the first predicate; ليس permits the same alternatives.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The accusative is also possible when the second item shares the first particle, as in ليس زيد ذاهبا ولا أخوك منطلقا and ما زيد ذاهبا ولا معن خارجا.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | rejects | Sībawayh rejects the claim that ما allows only nominative coordination: a second item can share the first ما even when the particle is not repeated.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A fresh clause after ما negates a separate state at the time of speaking; after كان, the negation can cover past and present, while ليس can also refer back to the first item.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The second predicate can be accusative when it relates to the first subject through a possessive pronoun, as in ما زيد كريما ولا عاقلا أبوه.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An unrelated predicate such as عاقل عمرو is raised because it does not relate to Zayd; the fronted predicate blocks accusative ما-governance.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أهل الحجاز | reports | The Hijaz dialect makes ما govern like ليس because the two particles share the meaning of negation.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After a fronted predicate, a fresh predicate such as ولا كريم أخوه is raised; unlike ما, ليس and كان can license accusative in that position.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | With a repeated subject after a fronted predicate, nominative is preferable; accusative is possible but weak because the repeated noun should normally be an implicit pronoun.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Suwād ibn ʿAdī’s verse shows that explicit repetition can nevertheless occur after a negated predicate.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A repeated explicit name is not equivalent to an attached pronoun; an unrelated overt phrase such as أبو زيد lacks the required connection and is disallowed.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ما أبو زينب ذاهبا ولا مقيمة أمها, the second predicate is raised because the mother is not related to the first subject.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In al-Aʿwar al-Shannī’s verse, مأمورها is attached to the broader referent الأمور, not to the masculine المنهيها; some instead link it to the latter and use genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r26] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some poets link مأمورها to منهيها, construing the latter through الأمور; Sībawayh compares Jarīr’s feminine agreement with a partitive antecedent.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r27] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī’s clause coordinates the verbal noun أن تعقرا with أن نردها, even though the injury is not itself the act of returning.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r28] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh allows the second phrase to be attached to the first by sense; al-Jaʿdī and Dhū al-Rummah support feminine agreement through the horses or winds understood as its referent.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لات only occurs with حين, with an implicit nominative and حين as its accusative object; unlike ليس, it cannot form ordinary subject predicates.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r30] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Accusative alternatives are possible for the coordinated predicates قاصرا and مستنكرا, paralleling other constructions after ليس or ما.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r31] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After ما كل سوادء تمرة, the second كل may be omitted; بيضاء is then genitive, though شحمة can also be accusative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r32] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Abū Dāwūd’s verse supports omitting the repeated كل; similarly, split coordination permits genitive or accusative after ما مثل عبد الله.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r33] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The same two case choices apply when the coordinated phrase is separated from its predicate, as in ما مثل عبد الله يقول ذاك ولا أخيه يكره ذاك.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لات is restricted to implicit constructions and cannot be inflected or used like ليس with an overt subject or plural subjects.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكالحرفما|تقولماعبداللهأخاكومازيدمنطلقا|وأمابنوتميم#38/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Even with حين, لات has limited distribution; Sībawayh compares it with لدن plus غدوة and tāʾ of oath, which are likewise restricted.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In an admonition with إياك, if نفس refers to the implicit subject, make أنت explicit; attaching نفس directly to the hidden subject is awkward.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl would not criticize إياك نفسك because the kāf is genitive.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | A trusted report records a Bedouin saying فإياه وإيا الشواب, an attested use of إيا with a following genitive form.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | إياك نفسك is poor when نفس is meant to modify the implicit subject; compare the bad imperative اذهب نفسك with اذهب أنت نفسك.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · auth
<<part 3 ends; continues in part 4>>

<<2:286 notes, part 4 of 0..33>>
or | holds | When the coordinated noun is another object of warning, it can follow إياك with wāw, as in إياك وزيدا والأسد.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Coordination with an implicit nominative subject is awkward without an overt أنت; with أنت, إياك أنت وزيد can attach either to the accusative or the implicit subject.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | The accusative coordination is better; coordinating to the hidden nominative is normally avoided except in poetry, as Jarir's verse shows.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Jarir's verse supplies a poetic exception to coordination with an implicit nominative subject.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | إياك زيدا is not allowed without a linking preposition or conjunction; the same applies when إياك is followed by an action.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | إياك أن تفعل is allowed when أن expresses the feared purpose or reason, as in ‘I warn you lest you do it’; it is not coordinated with the first noun.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكإياكأنتنفسكأنتفعلوإياكنفسكأنتفعل|فإنعنيتالفاعل#109/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Ibn Abi Ishaq is reported to permit a poetic إياك المراء by treating the repeated pronoun as a separate warning and supplying an unspoken verb.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With a topicalized noun followed by a direct question, ابتداء governs the noun and the interrogative clause is its predicate; in an embedded question, the matrix verb governs.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A clause introduced by أن is nominal: its verb completes the noun as a relative clause and has no independent government over the preceding noun.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In أزيد أن يضربه عمرو أمثل أم بشر, the مصدر clause is the topic and أمثل its predicate, not a finite verb governing زيد.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Comparatives and adjectives such as أكرم, أصدق, and خير are not verbs, so the noun in this interrogative comparison is nominative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A verbal noun after أشد is an ordinary noun of specification, like the accusative in ما أحسن زيدا, not an object governed by the comparative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a conditional answer is jussive, it cannot govern the topicalized noun; the noun is nominative, and the protasis is adverbial to the response.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | If إن directly precedes a noun in its protasis, the noun is accusative because the verb is most properly adjacent to إن.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | The verse of al-Nimr ibn Tawlab attests إن followed by an accusative noun in a conditional clause.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A poet may use إذا like إن: a jussive response makes the initial noun nominative; without that response relation it is accusative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With أيهم as a conditional noun, a jussive following verb is its predicate; the initial noun is therefore nominative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In أزيد إن يأتك تضربه, the suffix can only resume Zayd, because the topic needs a coreferential element in its predicate.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An interrogative particle attaches to the predicate and cannot intervene between a governor and its governed word.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After لم and لن a fronted object remains accusative; these negatives do not create the conditional structure that permits nominative topicalization.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | كل رجل is accusative before فاضرب because يأتيك is descriptive; أيهم is nominative when its clause is a conditional predicate, but can be accusative if it means ‘the one who.’
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A temporal adverb such as حين cannot by itself predicate something of a person; it can modify a clause that contains an event.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Without conditional force, زيدا يوم الجمعة أضرب is accusative; a temporal conditional clause can instead form a predicate, as in زيد إذا جاءني فأنا أضربه.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A fronted noun in this question pattern needs a resumptive pronoun in the following verb; omitting it makes the construction weak.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A noun completed by a relative clause remains nominative: رأيت is the relative clause, not a verb governing أخواك.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When a following verb clause describes a noun, it is not built on that noun as an object; a resumptive pronoun is best, though omission is attested.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Zayd al-Khayr's interrogative verse and the preceding anonymous verse attest clauses following a fronted time phrase in this descriptive pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Jarir's verse explicitly illustrates a descriptive clause with the resumptive pronoun omitted; another anonymous line supplies a similar example.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An indefinite active participle can function like a present or future verb and govern an object.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكزيدكممرةرأيتهوعبداللههللقيتهوعمروهلالقيتهوكذلك#63/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The definite participle means ‘the one who struck’; it behaves like a relative clause and therefore stays nominative rather than governing an object.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After a negative with a singular antecedent, the exception is normally accusative as a badal included in the set removed by the negation.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yūnus says Arabs treat من as indefinite in قل من يقول ذاك, supported by Rabba’s line where ما is also indefinite.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · أبو عمرو | prefers | Yūnus reports that Abū ʿAmr preferred nominative after القوم; some speakers use accusative by construing the exception with the affirmative clause.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The Qur’anic ولم يكن لهم شهداء إلا أنفسهم supports taking the exception as a badal from the negated noun, not from a collective subject. | mentions 24:6
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After a subordinate clause, accusative is the normal exception, while nominative is also possible by attaching to its implicit pronoun; Adī ibn Zayd’s line illustrates it.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Accusative is preferred because the exception is a badal from the negated noun, not from the nominative pronoun inside its descriptive clause.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nominative is also allowed in ما أظن أحدا فيها إلا زيدا and related clauses, like Adī ibn Zayd’s إلا كواكبها.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After an actual action such as ضربت only accusative is allowed: the point is that Zayd was among those struck, not that he alone says it.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Khalil argues that رأيته يقول and ظننته يقوله target what is known or thought, not a person as the object of an action such as striking.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكماأتانيأحدإلازيداومامررتبأحدإلازيدومارأيتأحدا#373/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أقل رجل says the exception is a badal from the initial phrase; قل رجل has the meaning of أقل رجل, while من can be indefinite.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمالكوزيداوماشأنكوعمرا|فإنماحدالكلامههناماشأنك#119/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ما شأنك وزيدا, attachment to the hidden pronoun is awkward and attachment to الشأن is ambiguous, so the construction is analyzed through an implied verb: ما شأنك وتناولك زيدا.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمالكوزيداو

ماشأنكوعمرا|فإنماحدالكلامههناماشأنك#119/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When the first name is overt, the following coordinated name can be genitive, as in the reported Arab examples ما شأن عبد الله وأخيه and ما شأن قيس والبر.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمالكوزيداوماشأنكوعمرا|فإنماحدالكلامههناماشأنك#119/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With ما أنت وزيد, nominative is more frequent and better; with ما شأن عبد الله وزيد, genitive is better because both are understood under شأن.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمالكوزيداوماشأنكوعمرا|فإنماحدالكلامههناماشأنك#119/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The accusative in ما لزيد وأخاه can be understood through an omitted كان شأن construction, which supplies the verbal relation.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمالكوزيداوماشأنكوعمرا|فإنماحدالكلامههناماشأنك#119/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | حسبك وزيدا permits the accusative because حسبك means كفاك; speakers supply an implicit verb rather than attach the noun to the hidden pronoun.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمالكوزيداوماشأنكوعمرا|فإنماحدالكلامههناماشأنك#119/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In ويلا له وأخاه and ويله وأباه, the accusative is licensed by the understood verb ألزمه الله, even though the verb is not stated.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمالكوزيداوماشأنكوعمرا|فإنماحدالكلامههناماشأنك#119/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | هذا لك وأباك cannot take an accusative second noun because the expression contains neither a verb nor a particle with verbal force.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Khalil analyzes يا أيها الرجل like يا هذا الرجل: الرجل describes هذا.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | If a descriptor that forms one name with a demonstrative is extended by a genitive or coordination, the extension is nominative because it is not itself addressed.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | يا أيها الجاهل ذو التنزى exemplifies a nominative genitive extension to the raised descriptor.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In يا أيها الرجل زيد أقبل, زيد takes tanwīn because the added mudaf is in a nominative position; tanwīn is omitted only in the accusative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In يا زيد الطويل ذو الجمة, ذو is nominative if it describes الطويل, but accusative if attached to Zayd.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ذا الجمة can coordinate to هذا with accusative but not to أي; ذا الرجل can describe أي because both are demonstrative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض العرب | reports | Some Arabs say يا هذا زيد is common in Ṭayyiʾ speech.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In يا زيد الناكي العدو وذا الفضل, ذا الفضل is accusative if attached to Zayd, but can form a new vocative if addressed to someone else.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أي needs an explanation and cannot stand alone, so it and الرجل form one name and the descriptor is nominative.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Demonstratives such as هذا، هؤلاء, and أولئك take definite-article descriptions like أي; this differs from a complete proper-name address followed by an afterthought.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ذا الجمة after يا هذا is apposition or coordination, not a description; it confirms an already completed address.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ibn Lūdhān’s يا صاح ياذا الضامر العنس and Ibn al-Abras’s examples show descriptive phrases following ذا.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ذا الجمة identifies ذا, but الضامر and الحسن are not identified by what follows; those phrases explain the respect in which the quality applies.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | الحسن is general and الوجه specifies what is beautiful; العنس likewise identifies the respect in which الضامر applies.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | يا هذا الحسن الوجه is remote, since the construction resembles a verb with its object, as in يا هذا الضارب زيدا.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكياأيهاالرجلوياأيهاالرجلانوياأيهاالمرأتان|فأى#290/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Khalil treats يا زيد الحسن الوجه like يا زيد الحسن; the following phrase does not become a second vocative.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Non-obligatory negation particles allow a noun before the verb, by analogy with interrogatives and conditionals; the clause after the noun supplies its predicate.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Sībawayh prefers analyzing such ليس clauses with an omitted element after ليس and a new topic, as in إنه أمة الله ذاهبة.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The Qur'anic clause إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر is an ordinary Arabic accusative-fronting construction like زيدا ضربته. | mentions 54:49
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some read ثمود accusative in وأما ثمود فهديناهم; Sībawayh says the reading does not conflict with the analysis because transmitted readings are sunna. | mentions 41:17
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With ما أنا زيد لقيته, accusative زيدا is available only on the analysis that also makes زيدا لقيته accusative; the intervening topic otherwise blocks it.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After إني, أنا, and ليتني, a fresh nominal or verbal clause can occupy the predicate position after the initial pronoun.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | كان does not govern a later noun as an ordinary verb would; the following clause can serve as its predicate and block separate verbal government.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | If كان has already taken its predicate, a following coordinated noun and clause can be accusative; if not, that clause is the predicate instead.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The object pronoun in حسبتني requires a predicate just as the name after كنت does; the following clause can supply that predicate.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The lām in قد علمت لعبد الله تضربه signals an explanatory predicate rather than coordination; omission of wāw has the same effect.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Marrār al-Asadī's verse attests an accusative alternative in poetic usage.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The accusative pattern uses a resumptive pronoun in the verb after the fronted noun.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Hadba ibn al-Khashram's line is cited as poetic evidence for nominal fronting under negation.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Zuhayr's line supplies another poetic example of a noun placed before the negative clause.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Jarir's line likewise supports the use of a fronted noun with negation.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Nominative is also possible, and Sībawayh says it is stronger because the clause can begin after negation and be built on the topic.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In the Hijazi dialect, ما works like ليس and therefore permits only the nominative construction.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some recited Muzahim al-Uqayli's line with أنا عارف nominative; Sībawayh allows an analysis on ليس or, more remotely, on the idiom كله لم أصنع.
[SIBAWAYH:وهىحروفالنفىشبهوهابحروفالاستفهامحيثقدمالاسمقبلالفعللأنهن#67/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | A reported view makes ليس govern like ما, but Sībawayh says this usage is rare and scarcely known.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The petitions are distinct approaches to prayer, though all seek entry into Paradise.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Calling God our mawla praises Him, draws the supplicant near, and thanks Him; mawla derives from wali and denotes guardianship.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r14] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Victory over unbelievers enables the law to stand, the Muslim word to prevail, and the way to obedience to remain open.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r15] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · جبريل | reports | Gabriel teaches Muhammad the petitions one by one and answers that God has granted each through the end of the sura.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r16] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · معاذ بن جبل | reports | Muadh ibn Jabal is reported to say amin after reciting the sura.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Ibn Atiyya links these senses to the root for something binding, such as a cord tying loads.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عاصم | reports | A reading transmitted from Asim has isran with damma on the hamza.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Those who came before are the Jews; al-Dahhak adds the Christians.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · قتادة | reports | Qatada asks not to be burdened with the same harshness as those before us.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الضحاك وابن زيد | reports | Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd understand the plea as asking not to be burdened with acts beyond capacity.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن جريج | reports | Ibn Jurayj interprets it as asking God not to transform believers into apes and swine.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · سلام بن سابور | reports | Salam ibn Sabur says the unbearable thing is sexual desire; al-Naqqash transmits this from Mujahid, Ata, and Mak'hul.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394#2/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو الدرداء | reports | Abu al-Darda seeks refuge from sexual desire for which there is no means of satisfaction.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري وغيره | reports | Al-Tabari and others take forgetting as neglecting obedience and error as intentional sin; involuntary forgetfulness and error are already excused.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r10] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عطاء | reports | Ata interprets the burden as transformation into apes and swine.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r11] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd also explains isr as a sin for which there is neither expiation nor repentance.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | prefers | Many scholars, including Ibn Atiyya, hold that the prayer concerns involuntary forgetfulness and unintentional error; he calls this correct.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · النبي | reports | Qatada says he was told the Prophet stated that God excused his community for forgetfulness and error.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddi says that after believers recited the prayer at its revelation, Gabriel told the Prophet God had granted it.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Believers feared the reckoning in 2:284 and seek protection from forgetfulness and error beyond human control; on this reading an impossible duty is possible. | mentions 2:284
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري والزجاج | reports | Al-Tabari and al-Zajjaj deny impossible duties: forgetting means omitted duties, error intentional disobedience, and the burden Israelite obligations and punishments.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري والزجاج | reports | For these authors the burden included killing themselves, cutting their bodies, bodily punishment for sins, and difficult covenants.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Akhṭa'a can describe intentional action as well as genuine mistake or deliberated action.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p394/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · قتادة ومجاهد وابن عباس والسدي وابن جريج والربيع وابن زيد | reports | These exegetes explain isr as a firm covenant or solemn pact.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Ibn Atiyya says Muadh's practice may be a Prophetic report, or sound analogy with al-Fatiha because both contain supplication.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبو مسعود عقبة بن عمرو | reports | Abu Masud Uqba ibn Amr transmits that reciting the last two verses at night suffices in place of night prayer.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · علي بن أبي طالب | reports | Ali says he doubts anyone who understands Islam would sleep without reciting the two verses.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p395/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · النبي | reports | The Prophet says he received the final verses from a treasure beneath the Throne, a gift no one before him received.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Wusʿ is less than ṭāqa: capacity is what a person can bear without being constrained; akhṭaʾnā means committing an error or sin.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The verse disproves the Mujabbira's allowance of obligations beyond ability: capacity lies within human power, beyond which effort is exhausted.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | rejects | The alternative that wusʿ means only what is permitted is mistaken: it makes the command circular, since every command itself permits the commanded act.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | A person receives the reward of obedience and bears the consequence of sins; both may be called earnings because they result from one's acts.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r13] TABRISI, d. 548 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan understands the prayer as an instruction to say these words, teaching believers how to supplicate.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r14] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Another reading supplies they say, presenting the words as reported praise and supplication.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو عبيدة | reports | Abū ʿUbayda says akhṭaʾa and khaṭiʾa are both Arabic forms, but the former can be sinful or non-sinful error while the latter means sin alone.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | An unnamed poet uses khaṭiʾū for sinning against what is right, witnessing the sin-specific sense of khaṭiʾa.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Iṣr means weight or burden; it can also denote a binding covenant or kinship tie.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · النابغة | reports | Al-Nābigha's poetry uses iṣr for the burden of protecting one's people from oppression.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · النابغة | reports | Al-Nābigha also uses iṣr to mean a covenant or binding promise.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · الكميت | reports | Al-Kumayt's verse uses āṣirat al-arḥām for the bond of kinship.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | God commands or forbids only what a person can do; another explanation says He requires ease rather than hardship and does not exhaust capacity.
[TABRISI:2:286#2/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · سفيان بن عيينة | reports | Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna calls it a good interpretation that God does not impose a person's full limit of capacity, which would exhaust their effort.
[TABRISI:2:286#3/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | One interpretation takes forgetting as abandoning obedience and error as committing sins, even deliberately; the prayer seeks forgiveness for neglected duties and wrongful acts. | mentions 9:67, 2:44
[TABRISI:2:286#3/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | The author cites 9:67 and 2:44 for nasiya meaning abandonment, and an unnamed poet who uses nāsiyan for leaving off spear thrusts in battle. | mentions 9:67, 2:44
[TABRISI:2:286#3/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | A second reading asks pardon if people expose themselves to circumstances that cause forgetfulness or error about a command or duty.
[TABRISI:2:286#3/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | A third reading means accidentally failing an obligation or unintentionally doing a forbidden act; the plea expresses humility even though such acts are not punished.

ISI, d. 548 · author | reports | This humble appeal resembles the following plea not to impose what people cannot bear, which may also be devotional.

[TABRISI:2:286#3/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والربيع والسدي | reports | One explanation asks God not to impose a duty people cannot carry out or punish them for abandoning or violating it.

[TABRISI:2:286#4/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Earlier communities were punished for sins, had lawful foods forbidden, and received heavier covenants and obligations; this community's lighter burden is a mercy. | mentions 4:160
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · النبي | reports | A well-known Prophetic report says whoever recites the final two verses of al-Baqara at night is sufficed for that night's vigil.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r11] TABRISI, d. 548 · عبد الله بن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿūd reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet reached the Lote Tree, received the five prayers and the final verses of al-Baqara, and his community's monotheists were forgiven except for grave sins.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن المنكدر | reports | Ibn al-Munkadir transmits from the Prophet that the final verses of al-Baqara are Qur'an and supplication and please the Merciful.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r13] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن عباس | reports | In al-Kalbī's tafsir report from Ibn ʿAbbās, an angel announces two lights not given to a prophet before—the Opening and the end of al-Baqara—and says reciters will receive their request.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r14] TABRISI, d. 548 · عبد الله بن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿūd says that when a man learned Sūrat al-Baqara, he became earnest and respected among the community.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The ban on good foods for the earlier community is illustrated by 4:160, which says they were forbidden lawful good things because of wrongdoing. | mentions 4:160
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | One explanation asks not to be burdened with crushing duties or trials, such as killing oneself as repentance for sin.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | A second explanation asks protection from punishment that people cannot endure in this life or the next.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | A third explanation treats this as devotional petition, though God does not impose on anyone a burden beyond their capacity.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The prayer asks God to pardon sins, cover errors, and show mercy through blessing in this world, pardon in the next, and admission to Paradise.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Mawlānā means our protector, the one entitled to direct our affairs, and our helper.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The final plea asks God to help believers overcome unbelievers by force and by the strength of their argument.
[TABRISI:2:286#4/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · النبي | reports | A report from the Prophet says that at every section of this supplication God answers, I have done so and granted it.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Linguistically, error is an act that occurs contrary to the actor’s intention.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | In legal usage, error is committing a prohibited act with the mistaken person’s intent.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · علي بن عبيد الله | reports | ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd Allāh distinguishes khāṭiʾ, who hits without intending, from mukhṭiʾ, who intends but misses.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r6] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Khaṭaʾ can mean an unintentional mistake. | mentions 4:92
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p92/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن فارس | reports | Ibn Fāris gives isr the senses of burden and covenant, and relates it to bonds of kinship or agreement.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p92/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Arabic usage can call any bond, kinship, or covenant an isr.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p92/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Al-Ḥuṭayʾa’s line describes people showing kindness without a bond or kinship.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p92/r4] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | A maʾṣar is where a watcher stops a passing animal to collect a toll; aṣartu-hu means I detained it.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p92/r5] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Some interpreters distinguish two Qurʾānic senses of isr: burden in 2:286 and covenant elsewhere. | mentions 3:81, 7:157
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p92/r7] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك، والسدي | rejects | These authorities take isr in 2:286 as a covenant; the author says this invalidates the two-sense division.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says that what accrues to a person is obedience and what accrues against them is disobedience.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو بكر النقاش | reports | Al-Naqqash says the wording “for her” points to good and “against her” points to evil.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · قوم | reports | One view distinguishes kasabat for a single occurrence and iktasabat for repeated acts over time.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · آخرون | reports | Another view treats kasabat and iktasabat as two forms with the same meaning, as in 86:17. | mentions 86:17
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | This prayer is God's instruction to people to say these words.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Ibn al-Anbari takes forgetting here as deliberate neglect, since involuntary forgetfulness is already exempt from sin; he likewise takes error here as intentional, though the word can also mean inadvertence.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس، مجاهد، الضحاك، السدي | reports | One interpretation of iṣr is a covenant.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346#2/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Another interpretation is a burden: a request not to impose the heavy obligations imposed on the Children of Israel.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس، قتادة | reports | Wusʿ means capacity.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | prefers | The verse means God does not impose what a person cannot do, since that would be impossible, like requiring a paralytic to run or a blind person to see.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | It is possible to impose a task a person cannot fulfill because of absent means, such as faith on someone eternally known not to believe; this verse concerns impossibility in itself.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The prayer later in the verse asks not to be burdened with what cannot be borne; if impossible obligations could never be imposed, that request would be pointless.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p346/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Ibn al-Anbari instead understands the request as asking not to be given a burdensome task, though it could be performed with strain; Arabs say they cannot bear looking at someone they actually can look at.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الضحاك، السدي، ابن زيد، الجمهور | reports | The first of five views understands this as asking not to be given deeds that are difficult and arduous.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الثوري عن منصور عن إبراهيم | reports | A second view takes the unbearable thing to be love.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · مكحول | reports | A third view identifies it as sexual desire.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · قوم | reports | A fourth view identifies it as inner thoughts and their whisperings.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · قوم | reports | The fifth view takes it as the punishment of Hell.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Anta mawlānā means “You are our protector.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Fa-nṣurnā means “help us.”
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p347/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · معاذ | reports | Muʿadh used to say “Amen” after finishing this surah.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | The Muʿtazila cite this verse and 22:78, 4:28, and the promise of ease to argue that God does not impose what a person cannot do. | mentions 22:78, 4:28
[RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their first premise is that people create their own acts: if God created the commanded act, the person could neither produce it again nor resist God's power; if God did not, the person could not bring it about.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | Their second premise is that ability precedes the act; otherwise an unbeliever commanded to believe would not be able to do so, making the command impossible.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أصحابنا | holds | Al-Rāzī's Ashʿarite colleagues say rational proofs establish that impossible commands do occur, so this verse must be interpreted.
[RAZI-FULL:v7p121#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | The first rational argument invokes God's eternal knowledge that one who dies in unbelief will never believe; that foreknown nonbelief is incompatible with belief, making the command appear to require a contradiction and likewise raising the problem of compulsion.
